label: Measured on open data

datasets.name: A dataset of neonatal EEG recordings with seizure annotations (Helsinki University Hospital)
datasets.credit: Stevenson NJ, Tapani K, Lauronen L, Vanhatalo S. A dataset of neonatal EEG recordings with seizure annotations. Scientific Data 6, 190039 (2019), https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2019.39. Data: Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4940267 (version 4), CC BY 4.0.

split: Split by baby before any modelling (seeded, stratified by whether a baby has any consensus seizure): 39 babies for training (229 seizure events), 16 for validation, which alone sets each design's alarm threshold (109 events), and 24 held out (113 events; 14 of them have seizures). Held-out babies were never used for training, feature scaling, thresholds or selection.
notes: Stage 2: all 79 babies of the record are used; this replaces the earlier subset file.
Feasibility result on one hospital's recordings, not clinical evidence; no design here is a medical device.

Result in one line: the best pooled figure is 16/113 held-out events (c2-h0-w4-s1, 632 gates, 2.075 false alarms per hour); the best worst-baby figure is 0.00, so every design misses every event in at least one held-out baby. These simple amplitude features do not separate seizures well across babies; the cloud shows that, not a working detector.

Label rule: a second is seizure when at least 2 of the 3 experts marked it. Consensus runs closer than 10 s are one event; events shorter than 10 s are not scored (alarms over them do not count as false).

Event matching: an event is caught when the design's alarm is on at any decision between its onset and its end plus 30 s. Decisions come every second at the end of an 8 s window. False alarms: alarm time outside every seizure (onset to end plus 30 s), with runs closer than 60 s merged, counts one false alarm per started 60 s, so an alarm that stays on keeps counting.

Worst-baby sensitivity is the lowest per-baby share of events caught among held-out babies with at least 2 events: 12 of 24 held-out babies qualify, with event counts [2, 2, 3, 3, 6, 6, 8, 9, 10, 16, 21, 25]. With so few babies it rests on one baby's count.
Each design's threshold is set on the validation babies only: the best mean per-baby sensitivity with at most 1.0 false alarm per hour on validation; held-out false alarm rates can differ.

Design: 6 integer features per channel (line length, mean absolute amplitude, zero crossings, high-frequency residual, and line length and residual relative to a causal 120 s background), 6-bit log-scaled; one tiny network shared by the channels (a single linear unit, or 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 hidden units with 4-bit activations), weights of 3, 7, 15 levels, 4 training seeds each; alarm when the maximum score over channels passes the threshold. Channels: 1 = C3-C4; 2 = C3-P3, C4-P4; 4 = adds T3-O1, T4-O2; 18 = double banana. Band-pass 0.5-30 Hz, 64 Hz.

Gates are from the chip lab's synthesis (simple 2-input gates) of the classifier only; the feature front end is not included. 433 of 433 designs compiled by the lab; 46 of them trained to a constant output (never alarm) and synthesise to 0 gates; 349 designs catch no held-out event at their validation threshold and are left off the frontier.

Verified: 4 designs (the frontier and the baseline) were checked bit for bit by the lab's simulation on held-out windows' integer features against the integer model; 4 of them were also formally proved equal to an independent model of the design for every input (level 2).

Development: the training recipe was revised once after a first stage-1 run (baby-balanced sampling, the validation threshold rule, one added feature), judged on validation figures, but that run's held-out figures had been printed in its log; nothing was selected on them afterwards. The false-alarm rule was then tightened once, because under the first rule an alarm that stayed on for long stretches scored as perfect; the run was repeated from training with the stricter rule, and no other change was made.
Baseline, scored the same way: line length of C3-C4 against a threshold set on validation babies: worst-baby 0.0, pooled 10/113, 0.296 false alarms per hour.
Spread across training seeds (same channels, size and weights): pooled sensitivity differs by a median of 0.00 (max 0.14); worst-baby sensitivity by a median of 0.00 (max 0.00).
Not done: power (layout and timing tools were not run, so power_uw_est is null), other hospitals' recordings, per-channel seizure localisation, and any tuning on the held-out babies.
